title: Watching the Orionids
summary_es: Maya llama a Leo para proponerle ir a ver la lluvia de estrellas de las Oriónidas lejos de las luces de la ciudad.
prediction_prompt: Two friends are planning a trip at night. What do you think they need to organise?

segments.speaker: maya
segments.text: Hey Leo, have you got a minute? I want to ask you about next week.

segments.speaker: leo
segments.text: Sure. What's up?

segments.speaker: maya
segments.text: You know the Orionids, the meteor shower? It's going to be at its best on Tuesday night.

segments.speaker: maya
segments.text: So I was thinking we could go and watch it together.

segments.speaker: leo
segments.text: Oh, nice! I've never actually seen a meteor shower.

segments.speaker: leo
segments.text: But where do you want to go? You can't see anything from here. There's way too much light.

segments.speaker: maya
segments.text: Exactly. That's the problem with the city: light pollution.

segments.speaker: maya
segments.text: So I found a place about forty minutes away by car.

segments.speaker: maya
segments.text: It's a small hill near a village called Ashford.

segments.speaker: maya
segments.text: There's a car park at the top, and there are almost no lights around.

segments.speaker: leo
segments.text: Forty minutes isn't bad. What time are we talking about?

segments.speaker: maya
segments.text: Well, the best time is after midnight, around two or three in the morning.

segments.speaker: leo
segments.text: Three in the morning? On a Tuesday? I've got work on Wednesday.

segments.speaker: maya
segments.text: I know, I know. But we don't have to stay all night.

segments.speaker: maya
segments.text: We could leave at half eleven, get there before midnight, and come back around two.

segments.speaker: leo
segments.text: Hmm, OK. That's not so bad. How many meteors are we gonna see? Like, hundreds?

segments.speaker: maya
segments.text: No, not hundreds. Maybe fifteen or twenty an hour, if we're lucky.

segments.speaker: maya
segments.text: But some of them are really bright. And did you know they come from Halley's Comet?

segments.speaker: maya
segments.text: They're basically tiny bits of dust the comet left behind.

segments.speaker: leo
segments.text: Wait, seriously? That's pretty cool. What about the weather, though? It's been raining all week.

segments.speaker: maya
segments.text: I checked the forecast this morning. Tuesday looks clear, but it's going to be cold, about four degrees.

segments.speaker: maya
segments.text: So bring a warm jacket and maybe a blanket.

segments.speaker: leo
segments.text: Got it. Should I bring my telescope?

segments.speaker: maya
segments.text: Actually, no. Meteors move too fast, and a telescope only shows you a tiny part of the sky.

segments.speaker: maya
segments.text: Just use your eyes. Oh, and don't look at your phone.

segments.speaker: maya
segments.text: It takes about twenty minutes for your eyes to get used to the dark.

segments.speaker: leo
segments.text: Twenty minutes? OK, no phone. I'll make some hot chocolate, then.

segments.speaker: maya
segments.text: Perfect. I'll pick you up at half eleven.

segments.speaker: leo
segments.text: Great. See you on Tuesday!

connected_speech.explanation_es: *have* y *you* se reducen (/həv/, /jə/) y *got a* se enlaza: las cuatro palabras suenan casi como una sola.
*to* se pronuncia /tə/ y se pega a *want*; *ask you about* va enlazado.
De *I've* (I have) apenas se oye la /v/ antes de *got*.
*going to* → *gonna* en habla informal; *are* casi desaparece (/ə/).
Leo es estadounidense: la *t* entre vocales suena como una *r* suave (flap).
Otra vez el flap americano: la *t* de *got* se enlaza con *it* como una *r* suave.
*for* y *your* son átonas (/fə/, /jə/); en inglés británico la *r* de *your* reaparece para enlazar con *eyes*.
En *used to* la /d/ desaparece: /juːstə/. Significa «acostumbrarse a».

connected_speech.phrase: pick you up at half eleven
connected_speech.explanation_es: Consonante + vocal se enlazan (*pick‿you‿up‿at*) y *at* es átona (/ət/).

glossary.def_en: an informal way to ask what is happening or what someone wants
glossary.example: Hey, what's up? You look worried.

glossary.def_en: a time when many small lights move quickly across the night sky
glossary.example: We stayed up late to watch the meteor shower.

glossary.def_en: much more than is good or needed
glossary.example: I spent way too much money this weekend.

glossary.def_en: too much artificial light at night, so you cannot see the stars well
glossary.example: Light pollution makes it hard to see the Milky Way.

glossary.def_en: an area or building where you leave your car
glossary.example: The car park was full, so we parked on the street.
glossary.note_es: Inglés británico. En EE. UU.: *parking lot*.

glossary.example: The film starts at half eight.

glossary.def_en: an object in space with a long bright tail of dust and gas
glossary.example: You can only see that comet every 76 years.

glossary.def_en: very small dry pieces of earth or other material
glossary.example: There was dust all over the old books.

glossary.def_en: a description of what the weather will probably be like
glossary.example: The forecast says it will rain tomorrow.

glossary.def_en: a large warm cover that you put over yourself
glossary.example: It was cold, so I took a blanket to the beach.

glossary.def_en: an instrument you look through to see things that are far away, like stars
glossary.example: She looked at the moon through her telescope.

glossary.def_en: to become familiar with something so it is no longer strange or difficult
glossary.example: It took me a month to get used to my new job.

glossary.def_en: to go somewhere by car to collect someone
glossary.example: Can you pick me up from the station at six?

options.text: To suggest a night out to see shooting stars
To ask him for a lift to work
To change the plans they made for Tuesday

tasks.rationale_es: Maya propone ir a ver la lluvia de estrellas (s3–s4). El telescopio aparece al final, pero es Leo quien lo menciona y Maya le dice que no hace falta.

tasks.prompt: How does Leo feel about the plan by the end of the conversation?

options.text: He thinks it's far too late on a work night and says no.
He agrees and offers to make a drink.
He wants to go another night.

tasks.rationale_es: Al principio le preocupa la hora (s13), pero acaba aceptando y se ofrece a preparar chocolate caliente (s27). La opción a describe solo su primera reacción.

tasks.prompt: How long does it take to drive to the hill?
tasks.rationale_es: *forty* lleva el acento en la primera sílaba (FOR-ty); *fourteen*, en la segunda (four-TEEN). Leo lo repite en s11.

tasks.prompt: When is the best time to see the meteors?

options.text: Just after the sun goes down

tasks.rationale_es: Maya dice que lo mejor es después de medianoche, hacia las dos o las tres. Las 11:30 es la hora de salida, no la mejor hora para verlas.

tasks.prompt: Leo has seen a meteor shower before.
tasks.rationale_es: Leo dice *I've never actually seen a meteor shower*. Ojo: *actually* significa «en realidad», no «actualmente».

tasks.prompt: How many meteors might they see?
tasks.rationale_es: Leo pregunta si verán cientos y Maya lo niega: *maybe fifteen or twenty an hour*.

tasks.prompt: Why does Maya tell Leo not to look at his phone?

options.text: So he doesn't wake up anyone in the village
So his eyes can adapt to the lack of light
Because there's no phone signal on the hill
Because the battery will die in the cold

tasks.rationale_es: Justo después explica que los ojos tardan unos veinte minutos en acostumbrarse a la oscuridad (s26). El frío se menciona, pero para recomendar ropa de abrigo.

tasks.prompt: What time will Maya pick Leo up?
tasks.rationale_es: En inglés británico, *half eleven* = *half past eleven* = 11:30. No es 10:30.

tasks.prompt: Maya thinks Leo should bring his telescope.
tasks.rationale_es: Maya dice *Actually, no*: los meteoros se mueven demasiado rápido y el telescopio solo muestra un trozo pequeño del cielo.

tasks.prompt: Maya has been to Ashford before.
tasks.rationale_es: Maya dice que ha encontrado el sitio (*I found a place*), pero no dice si ya ha estado allí. No hay información suficiente.

tasks.prompt: Complete the sentence with one word in each gap.
tasks.text: The Orionids are tiny bits of {{1}} that Halley's {{2}} left behind.
tasks.rationale_es: Maya explica que vienen del cometa Halley y que son partículas de polvo (*dust*) que dejó a su paso.

tasks.reference: Hmm, OK. That's not so bad. How many meteors are we gonna see? Like, hundreds?
accept_variants: Hmm, OK. That's not so bad. How many meteors are we going to see? Like, hundreds?
tasks.rationale_es: Reducción *gonna* y *are* casi inaudible antes de *we*.

tasks.reference: It takes about twenty minutes for your eyes to get used to the dark.
tasks.rationale_es: Formas débiles de *for* y *your*, y la /d/ que desaparece en *used to*.

tasks.reference: Perfect. I'll pick you up at half eleven.
accept_variants: Perfect. I will pick you up at half eleven.
Perfect. I'll pick you up at half past eleven.
tasks.rationale_es: Enlace *pick‿you‿up‿at* y la expresión británica *half eleven*.
